text:
sana: quick sync — finalizing the PRD acceptance criteria for audit-evidence. customers keep asking for 12+ months of raw request logs, but infra/cost/security pushback. need a concrete proposal we can ship as a beta.

mike: +1. can we do sampling + on-demand full retrieval for enterprise with a signed PO? that buys time and addresses cost.

amy: note: SOC2 auditors often want chain-of-custody + access proofs. sampling alone won't always satisfy. we need clear retention boundaries and an evidence export path with integrity checks.

josh: agree with amy. propose default: 90d raw request logs, 12mo derived audit bundle (redacted, hashed). enterprise addon: 12mo raw with KMS-wrapped keys and HSM-backed key IDs.

sana: ok. can someone draft the acceptance criteria lines? e.g., "evidence export includes integrity hash, requester id, KMS key metadata, and time window" — short bullet form we can paste into PRD.

amy: draft attempt:
- export contains: SHA256 of exported file, timestamp range, requestor identity, signed by platform KMS key id
- retention tiers: default-raw=90d, derived-audit=365d
- enterprise-raw=365d (opt-in, contractual)
- on-demand retrieval SLA: 7d for retrieval + 30d access window
- redaction: PII fields masked unless explicit customer opt-in

mike: minor edits: make SLA 5d for retrieval for Dedicated customers. also add: automatic sampling policy for low-risk customers: 1% sampled raw logs per day kept for 365d for trend analysis.

josh: include edge-case: customer requests deletion while audit export pending — must queue deletion until export completed + record a deletion event in audit bundle.

sana: love this. need the RFC to call out HSM/KMS mapping: what metadata we store (key id vs wrapped key), and how auditors verify signatures without access to private key. amy?

amy: we store KMS key id and the public certificate chain; exports include a detached signature (CMS) that can be verified with the public key. private key stays in HSM. add acceptance check: verification instructions included in export manifest.

sec_ops_bot: NOTE: retention changes require update to data inventory and privacy impact assessment. Filing: https://redwood.internal/pia/retention-2026-01

mike: question on encryption-at-rest for derived-audit bundles — do we encrypt with customer keys (CMEK) or platform key? pros/cons?

amy: recommend platform-encrypted by default + CMEK opt-in for enterprise. reason: operational simplicity for self-serve, stronger guarantees for contract customers.

josh: also add rollback behavior: if rollout fails, we must not switch retention backward silently. rollout plan: canary 5% orgs -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring on export failures and cost delta.

sana: acceptance criteria checklist for PRD (final):
- retention tiers documented and configurable
- export manifest includes integrity hash, KMS metadata, and verification steps
- enterprise opt-in path for raw 365d with CMEK/HSM mapping
- deletion semantics defined (queue + audit of deletion)
- SLA for retrieval per tier (5d dedicated, 7d enterprise standard)
- rollout plan with canary percentages + rollback criteria

amy: one more edge-case: archived exports older than retention must still be discoverable for legal holds. we need legal hold flag that pins records. add to checklist.

mike: cost note that product should show projected monthly cost delta per org when they opt into 365d raw. add UI acceptance: modal with cost estimate before enabling.

sana: perfect. I'll paste this into PRD and open RFC for review. can we aim to have draft RFC by EOD tomorrow? @mike @amy @josh pls +1 or flag blockers.

mike: +1

amy: +1

josh: +1, minor doc nit about wording on "derived-audit" -> maybe call it "evidence-bundle" in PRD.

sana: noted — will use "evidence-bundle". thanks all, will follow up with link to RFC when created.

sec_ops_bot: Reminder: schedule vulnerability review prior to GA. Ticket: VULN-2026-004
